chunks: Abū Baṣīr narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:
"Whoever withholds a qīrāṭ of zakat is not a believer nor a Muslim, and he will ask for return at the time of death
and this is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"Until, when death comes to one of them, he says: My Lord, send me back, so that I may do righteousness in that which I left behind."

key_terms.الرَّجْعَةَ: return, meaning being sent back to worldly life
key_terms.الزَّكَاةِ: zakat, the obligatory alms-tax due on wealth
key_terms.الْمَوْتِ: death, the moment of final departure from worldly life
key_terms.بِمُؤْمِنٍ: a believer, one possessing true faith
key_terms.قِيرَاطًا: a very small measured amount, indicating even a tiny portion
key_terms.مُسْلِمٍ: a Muslim, one in submission to Allah

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام say about withholding zakat and regretting it at death?
ai.summary: The hadith warns that withholding even a small amount of zakat is a grave spiritual failure that negates true faith and submission. It links this sin to the regret experienced at death, when the person wishes to return and perform righteous deeds. The Imam عليه السلام cites the Qur'anic verse to show that this plea for return reflects remorse over neglected obligations.
